name: Shared Decision-Making Drill — Deciding With the Patient
_note: Skill drill. Standard 4 metric keys re-pitched: medical_accuracy = balanced/plain-language options, clinical_reasoning slot = shared decision-making (the focus), communication_fluency = clarity of explanation.

anchors.70-80: Occasional minor errors; meaning always clear

anchors.90-100: Presents options with pros and cons in clear lay language, no jargon, no bias
anchors.70-80: Mostly balanced and plain; minor jargon
anchors.50-60: Explains options but unevenly or with some jargon
anchors.30-40: Mentions options only vaguely or pushes one heavily
anchors.10-20: Dictates a single plan; no real options given

anchors.90-100: Explicitly elicits values, checks understanding, and decides together with the patient
anchors.70-80: Asks the patient's preference and involves them in the choice
anchors.50-60: Some attempt to involve the patient but mostly leads them
anchors.30-40: Token involvement; effectively decides for the patient
anchors.10-20: No attempt to involve the patient at all

anchors.90-100: Explanations are smooth, well-structured, and easy to follow
Treats the patient as an equal partner; respects autonomy throughout
anchors.70-80: Respectful and warm; acknowledges the patient's views

checklist.item: presented more than one reasonable option
explained benefits and downsides in plain language
explicitly asked what matters to the patient / their preference
reached the decision together rather than dictating it
